quest.title: Leroy: Under Guard
quest.description: Molli still seems to want to go to Benoit's house...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000, Fruity Trio x3

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Oh, you two, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's name's Paimon, and {M#he}{F#she}'s {NICKNAME}. Just call us by our names from now on!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you come to see Benoit?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: That's right, but I didn't get a chance to speak to him... *sigh* Looks like I won't be able to finish my essay at this rate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your essay? Oh, right! You were doing good deeds because you had homework.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Hey, that's not true! I really do like Mr. Benoit. He's really... smooth! Yes, that's right, smooth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft, what kind of descriptor is that? You mean he's personable and a good communicator, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Anyway, please, Ms. Paimon, could you help me, please? If you don't, my essay's toast!

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: My tutor said that my essay about helping him to feed his cat was "Unpotentius and filled with genuine emotion from margin to margin," and she wanted me to write another.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? "Unpotentius"? Don't you mean "Unpretentious"? Anyway, Paimon gets it. So that's why you needed to come back.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Well, it is my homework, sure, but I really do like Mr. Leroy. He wanted me to say hi to my parents for him, and so I did.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: They were really upset when they heard his name though, and they didn't want me to come. I don't really know why...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if it's just for homework, it's easy, isn't it? You can just talk about how you fed the cat again!

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: But that would only be one line! That's too little, no way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll go with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right. You can feed the cat, and we'll clean the entrance and the rear of the house.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And when we're done, we'll knock on the door and talk to Benoit. That'll give you enough content to write about, right?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: That's right, we can do that! You're so smart, Ms. Paimon. Let me go feed the cat right now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Will this place do? C'mon, tell Paimon what's on your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's something off about that couple.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks so too. One of them talks a whole bunch, and the other barely says a word.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The timing of their appearance was too convenient to be a coincidence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean to say that they showed up just as Benoit was thinking about hiring some hourly help, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Euphrasie said that he was still hiring half a year ago, but in that time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This couple became his children.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right. Everything's just too deliberate... There's definitely something going on with this couple!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's something fishy about their relationship with Benoit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When we first met them a few days back, things still seemed fine, but there's something... awkward about the way they spoke today.

choices.text: He's being coerced by his son-in-law.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you talking about how that son-in-law guy gave him a look and made him go inside after he'd only said one or two things?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that you mention it, Paimon kinda gets where that confused feeling was coming from.

choices.text: Benoit's daughter is coercing him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon didn't quite think that far, but the way she spoke sure did give Paimon goosebumps...

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: #Ms. Paimon, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, I've fed the cat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice! Okay, let's go see Mr. Leroy.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: I'm worried, though. Maybe he won't come out? When I've come by to see him lately, he hasn't even spoken to me.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Before you arrived, I went and knocked, but just as he came out, that scary son-in-law of his came and dragged him back inside.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: He then gave me some sweets and told me to go back to my parents. Then he shut the door.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez. Benoit's such a chill guy, so why are his family members such a chilly bunch?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Mr. Leroy's son-in-law said that Mr. Leroy was ill and couldn't see me, but I thought he looked fine, so why couldn't he speak to us?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Honestly, I'm more worried about Mr. Leroy than I am about my essay.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: He must feel terrible if he's ill. Mama told me that sick people need our care and concern.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: So, could you come with me to ask that son-in-law what sort of illness Mr. Leroy has?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Maybe he ate too much cake, or he slept without a blanket? I can ask my parents about what to do!

choices.text: Regardless, let's knock on the door first.

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: I know, I'm just... a bit scared of that scary son-in-law, because he's... well, scary. Could you help me speak to him?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't be afraid, Molli. We've got this.

choices.text: Well, we made an agreement, didn't we?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Athos, the man you saw before, opens the door and walks out.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: You again? What in the world do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could we ask if Benoit's home? We heard he fell ill, so we're kinda worried about his health.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: My father is home, but he's in no condition to be receiving guests.

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Could we ask what he's come down with? I could ask my parents to help get him some medicine.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: No need. We'll buy what medicines are needed ourselves — not that he has any lack of medicine, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're just concerned for his health. You don't have to be so cold...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Athos just doesn't want to let us see Benoit!)

choices.text: (This is past cold, he's downright frigid...)

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: You concern yourself too much with business that is not your own. Very well. Was there anything else? If not, I'll be heading back.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: What is it?

choices.text: Is Benoit really ill?

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Of course he is. Very seriously, in fact. Morticia and I will think of something, though. There's no need for you — or anyone else, for that matter — to worry.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Athos, what's that disturbance outside?

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Nothing, Morticia, just a few kids saying that they want to see Dad.

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: You really do get along well with children, don't you, Dad?

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Well, since these kids want to see you, why don't you go say hello to them?

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: ...I'd like to... Can I?

response.speaker: Morticia
response.text: Of course you can, Dad. You're in charge.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The door opens and Benoit slowly emerges.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Ah, it's you again, little ones. You're back.

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: How are you feeling, Mr. Leroy?

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Me? *cough* Oh, I'm not doing quite so fine, but not to worry, I'm doing my best to rest up.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: My daughter and son-in-law are taking very good care of me, so all is well — just run along home, if you would.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Are you sure you're alright, Dad? If it's too much for you, you should go back inside.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Benoit sees Athos give him a meaningful glance before silently going back indoors.

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: Well? So you've seen him for yourselves, then. My father really is unwell. Does that satisfy you? If there's nothing else, I'm going back inside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Athos ignores all of you.

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: Well, at least we got to say a few words to Mr. Leroy. *sigh* I do hope he gets better soon.

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: Looks like I caused trouble for other people, Ms. Paimon. That... wasn't what I wanted...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't think that way! You weren't any trouble at all! In fact, Paimon thinks that Athos guy is the real problem here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. The entire time, he was just...

choices.text: You should go home first, Molli.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Eh? {NICKNAME}, you...

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: True, I should head back as well. My parents don't like it when I come here, you know? They'd get mad if they knew I came today...

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: I don't know if we'll get to see Mr. Leroy again. I really wanted to tell him that his snacks were super tasty.

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: Well, could you help me tell him that if you see him — after he gets better, I mean?

choices.text: No problem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon's, too!

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: #Alright. Thank you, {M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Molli
response.text: I've gotta go home now. See you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Paimon noticed you had "I've got something to say" written all over your face as soon as she looked at you!

choices.text: Let's talk over there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure, let's go talk somewhere else.

choices.text: Best not to speak too loudly right here.
You have my word.
Paimon and I will be heading back as well.
Why are you trying to prevent us from seeing Benoit?

response.speaker: Athos
response.text: And why must I allow completely unrelated people to see my father? Like I said earlier, he's in no condition to see guests.

choices.text: (He sure turned down the temperature quickly...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The way this couple deals with outsiders doesn't sit right with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly. They were nice enough when we first met them, but they sure turned rotten quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They were only friendly to us when their father was around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Let Paimon think. That's true. The first time we met, it was right after Benoit went inside that his son-in-law told us not to come around again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They're faking it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why would they pretend to be friendly in front of their dad? There's gotta be a reason for it...

talks.objective: Go to the side and talk with Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, that's all I've got for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Um, {NICKNAME}... Do you think Benoit's in some kinda danger?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, Paimon's got a bad feeling about this. Should we report it to the Maison Gardiennage?

choices.text: We've got no evidence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, that's true, that's true. But in the end, we're here to help him, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Molli asked us to tell Benoit that his snacks were super tasty, and we gave her our word.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And our word is our sacred bond.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon knows you always keep your promises! Well, you've got a good brain, too, so what's our next move?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's do some investigating.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, let's get to the bottom of this case! Hmm... What should we investigate, specifically?

choices.text: The identity of the couple.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That's right! Look out, world — Ace Detectives Paimon and {NICKNAME} are going to expose the truth!

choices.text: The couple's goals.
How Benoit feels about them.
The situation is still pretty murky.
We don't know how Benoit feels about all this.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Have you been sleeping well lately, Dad? Still suffering from insomnia?

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm much better. Don't even have nightmares nowadays...

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (The voices of the Leroy family grow less distinct...)

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: Nana, Nana, why is Mr. Leroy ignoring me? Do you know why?

dialogues.speaker: Molli
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Ms.} {NICKNAME}, could you do the knocking?

dialogues.speaker: Door
dialogues.text: (Nobody's answering, and there are no sounds from inside.)
